Arterial and skin fragility characterize vascular EDS; intestinal rupture is a minority complication, and joint laxity alone does not establish locomotor damage.
Rickettsial infection of vascular endothelium causes small-vessel vasculitis; the transient exanthem does not establish lasting skin damage.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disease; respiratory weakness, dysphagia and ptosis do not establish separate lung, intestinal or eye injury.
Immune-complex cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis causes recurrent purpura; elevated polyclonal globulins do not establish a blood-cell disorder.

Protozoal infection, predominantly reproductive tract disease; damaging urinary involvement is not established across the umbrella.

Inherited hepatobiliary bile-acid handling disorder; malabsorption reflects altered bile availability rather than intrinsic bowel injury. Rickets frequency is unspecified.
Multiple peripheral nerve sheath tumors define the disease; skin ancestry does not establish common independent skin involvement.

Oral and digital malformations define OFD17; TOF and renal hypoplasia each 1/1. CNS hypomyelination and hearing loss also 1/1, omitted at cap; single-case evidence.
Mitochondrial disorder causing cerebellar degeneration; ophthalmoparesis, abnormal saccades and ptosis reflect neurologic motor dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye injury.
Primary skeletal dysplasia involving ulnar and other metaphyses; dental abnormalities and kidney stones occur in only 5-29%.
Chondrodysplasia and gonadal endocrine failure define it; CNS hypoplasia occurs in 3/4 and ocular malformations in 2/2. Nail dysplasia omitted at cap.
Meningeal tumor affecting the supratentorial brain.
Tumor originates in a uterine supporting ligament, part of the reproductive system rather than locomotor connective tissue; ancestry does not override its site.
